1. `viewportSync()` checks `nearBot()` only **after** `setIBH()` changes the scroll geometry, so growing or shrinking the input bar can knock the user off the bottom without re-sticking the view.

2. `goBot()` immediately returns when `nearBot(4)` is true, so an explicit click on the “scroll to bottom” button can become a no-op during tiny offset drifts instead of forcing a final snap.

3. `highlight()` finds the match in normalized text but slices the original string using the normalized query length, so accented Hungarian text can be highlighted at the wrong character boundaries.

4. `md()` truncates oversized text with `String.slice()`, which can split surrogate pairs and corrupt astral Unicode characters.

5. The fenced-code regex in `md()` only handles the simplest triple-backtick form, so valid Markdown edge cases such as fence text inside code, alternate fence lengths, or missing trailing newlines are misparsed.

6. The inline-code regex in `md()` cannot handle escaped backticks or multi-backtick spans, so legitimate Markdown code spans break.

7. The emphasis parsing in `md()` is regex-order dependent and not structurally aware, so overlapping or nested italic/bold sequences can be mangled.

8. The Markdown link regex in `md()` breaks on URLs that contain `)` and on nested brackets inside link text.

9. The list parser in `md()` is flat-only, so nested lists and continuation paragraphs are destroyed.

10. `safeUrl()` rejects normal relative links like `./page` or `docs/readme.html`, so valid Markdown links silently remain inert text.

11. `flush()` re-renders the entire assistant message HTML from scratch on repeated stream updates, which makes long answers degrade toward quadratic-time rendering and causes avoidable layout churn.

12. `compress()` converts most still images to JPEG unconditionally, so transparent PNGs lose transparency and non-photographic assets can visibly degrade.

13. `compress()` recompresses even already-small images, so quality loss can happen without meaningful size savings.

14. `compress()` does not handle EXIF orientation, so photos from phones can render rotated incorrectly.

15. `compress()` exempts WebP entirely, so oversized static WebP uploads are never resized.

16. `handleFiles()` treats every non-image upload as text, so binary files such as PDF, DOCX, and ZIP are misread or fail in the wrong way.

17. `handleFiles()` has no attachment size limits, so a single large file or many files can freeze the UI and explode request size.

18. `send()` wraps attached text files inside triple-backtick fences without escaping fence content, so an attachment that already contains triple backticks can corrupt the generated payload.

19. `send()` clears the textarea and attachments before the request has succeeded, so a hard failure destroys the prepared draft instead of preserving it.

20. `streamReq()` leaves a partially rendered assistant bubble in the DOM when a transport error occurs, then creates a new bubble on retry, so one logical response can fragment into multiple visible attempts.

21. `streamReq()` has no retry cap, so repeated connection failures can trigger an endless retry loop.

22. Retries reuse the same payload after partial streaming failure without reconciling prior partial output, so duplicate or conflicting assistant fragments can accumulate in the transcript.

23. For non-OK HTTP responses, `streamReq()` adds an error bubble but provides no retry control, unlike successful assistant messages.

24. `stop()` aborts the request but leaves any already-rendered partial assistant output in an unfinished visual state, even though aborting the fetch is only the transport side of cancellation.[1]

25. The SSE reader is not a real SSE parser: it splits on single newlines and assumes one complete JSON object per `data:` line, so multiline SSE events or unusual framing will be mishandled.

26. The typing indicator appears only after the HTTP response has started, so long request setup time shows no loading feedback even though the composer has already switched to stop mode.

27. `loadSid()` reconstructs historical user messages from `content` only, so past uploads come back as raw fenced code blocks instead of the original “message + file chips” presentation.

28. `loadSid()` discards original `rawText` and attachment metadata, so historical user messages cannot be faithfully edited or resent after reload.

29. What the user sees immediately after sending a file message is not what history later replays, because the live view shows filenames while the stored message body contains full embedded file contents.

30. `delSession()` deletes locally first and ignores backend delete failure, so client and server history can diverge.

31. `loadSid()` clears the current conversation before the replacement history has loaded, so a failed load leaves the user staring at a blank thread.

32. `loadSid()` suppresses stale rendering with `loadGen`, but it never aborts the superseded network request, so wasted requests still run to completion.

33. `markDeleted()` and `applyDeleted()` identify messages by text plus image count, so duplicate messages with the same text and the same number of images can be confused.

34. The deletion replay scheme stores DOM index and duplicate occurrence count, both of which are unstable across edits and history changes, so replayed deletions are not robust.

35. `renameSession()` falls back to raw selector interpolation when `CSS.escape` is unavailable, so a session id containing selector metacharacters can break lookup.

36. `copyText()` falls back to `document.execCommand("copy")`, which is deprecated and unreliable in constrained browsing contexts.

37. `persistHist()` silently swallows storage failures, so pin, rename, or delete operations can appear to work and then disappear on reload.

38. Repeated `search_start` events append repeated source bars to the same assistant bubble, because the code never checks whether a prior search bar already exists.

39. `search_done` assumes `.srch-bar` exists under `curr._srch`, so malformed or out-of-order search events can trigger a null dereference.

40. `streamReq()` never explicitly releases the body reader; `getReader()` locks the stream until the reader is released, so this implementation relies on implicit teardown instead of explicit reader lifecycle cleanup.[1]

41. `syncMsgs()` rebuilds the canonical `msgs` array from the current DOM, so presentation state becomes the source of truth instead of the message model.

42. `attach()` stores message references only on DOM nodes, so removing nodes can orphan message metadata that is not mirrored elsewhere.

43. `errBubble()` can append multiple stacked error bubbles to the same message group, producing redundant noise after repeated failures.

44. The long-press context-menu implementation can race native touch behaviors because it does not suppress them early enough.

45. `ibWrap` blurs the textarea on any sufficiently downward swipe, so normal editing/scroll gestures can dismiss the keyboard unexpectedly.

46. `handleFiles()` processes files sequentially with `await` inside the loop, which unnecessarily serializes image conversion and file reading work.

47. The code converts uploads to base64 data URLs eagerly, which inflates memory usage and DOM weight compared with Blob/Object URL handling.

48. The image-removal handler deletes by `imgs.indexOf(url)`, so duplicate identical image attachments are removed by first-match lookup instead of instance identity.

49. `streamReq()` truncates `bufText` to the last 256000 characters, so very long assistant answers silently lose their beginning.

50. Unlike the initial `md()` input truncation path, the streaming truncation path adds no visible warning, so content loss in long assistant messages is silent.

51. `renderHist()` rebuilds the full history list on every relevant state change instead of patching changed rows, which scales poorly as conversation count grows.

52. The global `Ctrl/Cmd+K` handler fires regardless of focus context, so it hijacks a common shortcut even while the user is typing in the textarea.

that’s all.
